results.summary: This is a testchip containing a 16x32 single-port OpenRAM SRAM macro that uses two-phase clocking to avoid hold violations. It includes a scan chain for testing and supports byte write masking via the bidirectional pins. The design operates at clock frequencies up to 250 MHz and is controlled through dedicated inputs for clocks, chip select, write enable, and scan signals. No external hardware is required, but a scan chain tester may be used to verify functionality.

A fuzzy search engine that finds the best matching word in a dictionary using the bit-vector Levenshtein distance algorithm. It communicates with a host via SPI and requires an external QSPI PSRAM module to store the dictionary. Silicon testing confirmed it works but encountered a pinout mismatch with the v3 demo board, forcing a software SPI implementation limited to 500 kHz. The design is based on a 2003 paper by Heikki Hyyrö and is intended for applications needing approximate string matching.

A simple processing element (PE) implemented in VHDL. It takes two 4-bit inputs and a 3-bit operation selector, and produces a 4-bit result. The documentation is minimal, only stating to 'send in data' for testing. The exact operations or architecture are not described, so its capabilities are unclear.

Implements a simple PLC-style programmable logic controller in Verilog that reads eight digital inputs and drives eight digital outputs based on programmed control rules. It mimics the scan cycle of a PLC: read inputs, execute logic, update outputs. The design can be used with switches and LEDs for testing, and optional external hardware includes buttons and relays. It is a combinational or sequential design depending on configuration and is intended for prototyping small automation tasks.

A pulse width encoder that generates a digital pulse of programmable width based on a 4-bit input and control signals. An FSM coordinates the pulse generation across idle, counting, and done states. The design is fully synchronous and includes a testbench for simulation. It has no mandatory external hardware and can be used in larger digital systems.

A 4-bit R2R digital-to-analog converter that converts a 4-bit input signal to an analog output voltage. The design is implemented in analog and has one analog output pin. It requires an external signal source (e.g., ADALM2000 in digital mode) to provide the 4-bit input. The documentation is very brief, describing it as similar to an example design.

A test chip for evaluating mismatch in a simple CMOS beta multiplier current source. It contains 16 identical cells (eight oriented one way and eight rotated 90 degrees) whose outputs are combined into a single analog output. Individual cells can be disabled via digital inputs. Silicon measurements show an output current mean of 0.7uA with a standard deviation of 0.1uA, and no statistical difference due to orientation. External precision current measurement equipment is required.

Converts between binary, binary-coded decimal (BCD), and densely packed decimal (DPD) formats for values from 0 to 999. The design supports read and write operations via dedicated control pins and bidirectional data pins. It includes a Python test script that verifies conversions in all directions. External hardware is optional, as the design can be used with any input and output devices.

An ALU for the five operators of the INTERCAL programming language, including unary AND, OR, XOR, interleave, and select. It features two 32-bit registers and supports reading and writing bytes via address and selector pins. The design is intended for educational and novelty purposes, with extensive documentation and test cases. It can be used without external hardware, though a microcontroller is recommended for driving inputs and reading outputs.

A VGA screensaver that displays a bouncing logo with an animated color gradient, similar to the classic DVD screensaver. It supports a tiling mode and solid color mode via input pins, and can optionally be controlled with a Gamepad Pmod. The design outputs VGA signals for a 640x480 display and requires a TinyVGA Pmod for connection to a monitor. It is a fun visual demo with minimal external hardware.
